catalog_quote: 2.2 Suprasegmental phonology. Shinekhen Buryat has two accent systems: pitch accent and stress accent. Both systems are phonologically indistinctive, and clitics are not accentuated. a. Stress accent. The initial syllable is stressed. If VV (long vowel or diphthong) are found in other syllables, the syllable that has VV is stressed. E.g. xórgan 'lamb', teméen 'camel', gasʲóon 'bitter'. b. Pitch accent. V1 of the last syllable are pitched higher. E.g. xorgaꜜn 'lamb', temeꜜen 'camel', jabxa '(someone) will go'. [fn. 2:] 'ꜜ' indicates pitch fall. If the last syllable has neither V2 nor C2 (like jabxa presented above), the pitch does not fall. ... [p. 138:] Shinekhen Buryat is spoken by the Shinekhen Buryat people ... who inhabit the region around the Shinekhen river basin in Hulunbuir ... City, Inner Mongolia, China ... sources.citation: Poppe, N. 1932. Skizze der Phonetik des Bargu-Burjätischen. Asia Major (first series) 7(3): 307-378.
sources.quote: 'Der dynamische Akzent, welcher hier nicht bezeichnet wird, da er immer auf der ersten Silbe ruht, ist ebenso wie im Khalkhamongolischen sehr kraeftig ... Ausser dem dynamischen Akzent besitzt das Wort auch einen musikalischen Akzent, welcher auf die letzte Silbe faellt.' I.e. fixed initial dynamic stress (no long-vowel attraction mentioned) plus a final-syllable musical accent. NOTE: this describes New Barga (Sine-Bargu) as recorded c. 1930, not the Shinekhen Buryat (Aga-Buryat emigrant) variety our record codes; Glottolog files it under chin1476 but it is a different lect.
sources.locator: sec. 25 'Akzent', pp. 344-345 (PDF sheet 20 of 37, two-page spreads); p. 307 identifies the variety as Sine-Bargu ('Neu-bargu') Banner Mongols of NW Manchuria
sources.note: Glottolog's only 'phonology'-typed ref for chin1476; sec. 25 gives fixed-initial dynamic stress + final musical accent, but for New Barga, a different lect under the same glottocode -- relevant only as an identity/caution note, not for recoding.

sources.citation: Yamakoshi, Yasuhiro. 2003. シネヘン・ブリヤート語の音韻概説 [An Outline of the Shinekhen Buryat Phonology]. Languages of the North Pacific Rim 10 (ELPR A2-033): 69-86. Osaka Gakuin University.
sources.quote: p. 82: Shinekhen Buryat, like the other Mongolic languages, has no meaning distinctions by accent and forms a so-called fixed-accent system. p. 83 (5.1) reviews the two positions on Mongolian/Buryat accent: A. stress accent, either (a) always on the first syllable (Schmidt 1832, Luvsanvandan et al. 1966) or (b) basically first syllable but moving to a non-initial syllable containing a long vowel or diphthong (Poppe 1951, 1960, Street 1963); B. pitch accent (Hattori 1951, Kakudo 1982).
